text:
Maria Chen: Hey team — onboarding Neptune Health for BYOK. They want to use Azure Key Vault for data keys and GCP KMS for signing keys. Asking about envelope encryption support and any RBAC gotchas.
Joe Patel: welcome! we support envelope encryption. main things: ensure customer can create/unwrap keys and we can call Encrypt/Decrypt or GenerateDataKey, depending on flow.
Anna Gomez: do we have documented required permissions per provider? I remember needing keywrap for AKV + iam.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign for GCP.
Nate R.: quick checklist i usually send: 1) key creation policy (no auto-rotation unless they manage) 2) service principal/sa with exact roles 3) audit logging enabled 4) network restrictions if private deployment
Lee Park: Azure specifics: need "Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/keys/*" actions for our managed identity, or grant the App Registration "Key Permissions: WrapKey, UnwrapKey, Get" under Access policies if using classic. For RBAC-based access control on AKV (recommended), assign "Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User"? double-check the role name.
Maria Chen: Neptune asked about using a customer HSM (MHSM) vs soft keys. We told them MHSM is supported but we need the key export disabled and Get/Unwrap allowed. Is there an additional validation for MHSM flags?
Anna Gomez: For MHSM we validate key attributes: key_ops include unwrapKey/wrapKey, key_type RSA-HSM or EC-HSM, and hsm=true. Also ensure key has not been marked exportable. We run a quick GOV API check: ``GET /keys/{key-name}?api-version=7.3`` and assert "key.kty" contains "HSM" and "attributes.exportable": false.
Joe Patel: GCP side: need roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter for data key ops or roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier for signing. If they're using separate keys (data vs signing), we'll need both service account bindings and the key resource names in their onboarding form.
Maria Chen: They also asked about rotation windows. What's our recommended cadence and how we handle rotation?
Nate R.: recommend customer rotate CMKs every 90-365 days depending on compliance. For envelope keys (DEKs) we rotate more frequently on our side. Our flow: we fetch a new data key via KMS GenerateDataKey, re-encrypt DEK under the new CMK, swap pointer in metadata, and keep previous CMK as a fallback for 30 days. Document that 1) we need decrypt rights on old key during transition and 2) customer must not disable old CMK until fallback window passes.
Anna Gomez: add note: for Azure soft-delete + purge protection can prevent accidental key deletion; ask them to enable retention so we can decrypt during rollbacks.
Lee Park: audit logging: require tenant-level diagnostic settings for Azure Key Vault -> send logs to customer Log Analytics / Event Hub or storage account. For GCP, enable Cloud Audit Logs for Cloud KMS. We need their logs for incident triage.
Maria Chen: Neptune is using Private deployment (VPC) — they asked if our key access originates from within their VPC or from our control plane. How do we phrase that?
Joe Patel: control plane coordinates key usage but actual KMS calls originate from the runtime in their environment for Private (no egress from their VPC to our hosted infra). We'll document flow: runtime (in customer's VPC) authenticates with customer KMS using provided SA / managed identity, we never ship CMKs or DEKs out of their network except for wrapped ciphertexts.
Maria Chen: they hit an error during validation: "403 PermissionDenied: Permission 'cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get' denied". They pasted logs. Any quick debug tips?
Nate R.: common: SA doesn't have roles bound to the specific key resource—check IAM on the key ring and key version. Also ensure the service account email in our onboarding form matches the one in their IAM policy.
Anna Gomez: share quick command to verify on GCP: ``gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT_ID --flatten="bindings[].members" --filter="bindings.role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter" --format="json"``
Maria Chen: they want sample config to paste into their infra repo. Can we give them minimal snippet for private deployment KMS config?
Joe Patel: here's a minimal YAML we use (they can paste and redact IDs):
```
redwood_kms:
  provider: azure
  key_resource_id: "/subscriptions/SUBSCRIPTION_ID/resourceGroups/RG/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/VAULT/keys/KEYNAME"
  auth:
    type: managed_identity
    client_id: "<managed-identity-client-id>" # optional for user-assigned
  rotation:
    fallback_days: 30
    auto_rotate: false # customer-managed CMK rotate handled externally
```
If using GCP replace provider + resource_id: "projects/PROJECT/locations/global/keyRings/RING/cryptoKeys/KEY" and auth.type: service_account_key (or workload identity).
Lee Park: also include verification steps: 1) call Encrypt/Decrypt or GenerateDataKey via az CLI / gcloud 2) check runtime logs for successful Unwrap during startup 3) verify audit logs contain request id we see in runtime.
Maria Chen: perfect. can someone drop the docs link and I'll forward to Neptune?
Anna Gomez: https://docs.redwood.ai/private/byok-kms (internal link) :point_right: section "provider-specific checklist" has the step-by-step. I'll add the MHSM validation snippet later.
deploy-bot: Added onboarding ticket #ONB-4239 to the tracker and assigned to Maria Chen.
Maria Chen: thanks everyone — i'll follow up after they try the sample YAML. :thumbsup:
